# frozen_string_literal: true

require "securerandom"

# Rack middleware that ensures every response carries an X-Request-Id header.
#
# If the incoming request already has an X-Request-Id (e.g. set by a load
# balancer or upstream proxy), it is reused so the id can be traced across
# services. Otherwise a new UUID is generated. The id is also exposed to the
# app via env["request_id"].
#
#   use RequestId
class RequestId
  HEADER     = "x-request-id"           # Rack 3 requires lowercase header names
  ENV_KEY    = "HTTP_X_REQUEST_ID"
  MAX_LENGTH = 255
  VALID_ID   = /\A[\w\-.:]+\z/          # keep untrusted ids out of logs/headers

  def initialize(app)
    @app = app
  end

  def call(env)
    request_id = sanitize(env[ENV_KEY]) || SecureRandom.uuid
    env["request_id"] = request_id

    status, headers, body = @app.call(env)
    headers[HEADER] = request_id
    [status, headers, body]
  end

  private

  def sanitize(id)
    return nil if id.nil? || id.empty? || id.length > MAX_LENGTH
    id.match?(VALID_ID) ? id : nil
  end
end

I wrote the middleware in `request_id.rb` and ran a quick check that covered all three cases below.

To use it, add `use RequestId` to your `config.ru`.

- **Reuses an incoming id:** if the request already has an `X-Request-Id` (for example, from a load balancer or proxy), that same id goes on the response. This lets you trace a request across services.
- **Generates an id otherwise:** when there's no incoming id, it creates a new random one with `SecureRandom.uuid`.
- **Rejects bad incoming ids:** if the incoming id is empty, longer than 255 characters, or contains anything other than letters, digits, `_`, `-`, `.` or `:`, it's replaced with a new UUID. This stops a client from injecting line breaks into headers or logs.
- **Shares the id with your app:** the id is stored in `env["request_id"]` so your code can use it, for example in logging.
- **Header name:** the header is written in lowercase (`x-request-id`), as Rack 3 requires. Header names aren't case-sensitive, so clients still see the same header.
